question: How can intrinsic dimension be estimated when distances take discrete values, so nearest-neighbor ratios and infinitesimal volume-growth assumptions break down?

key_findings.claim: I3D estimates dimension from counts in two finite-radius discrete balls using the exact dimension-dependent growth of shell volume.
key_findings.evidence: Under locally constant density, neighborhood counts are modeled as Poisson variables whose mean is density times a discrete ball-volume formula. Conditioning on the outer count yields a likelihood for the inner/outer count ratio and an equation whose root estimates dimension.

anchors.section: Supplement analytic continuation of lattice volume

key_findings.claim: On uniform square lattices, I3D is more accurate near the minimum distance scale than continuous-metric, box-counting, and fractal-dimension alternatives.
key_findings.evidence: Two- and six-dimensional lattice experiments show that continuous estimators cannot resolve the staircase shell structure at small radii, whereas the discrete ball model tracks ground truth over a useful radius window. Model-validation plots identify where its assumptions cease to fit.

key_findings.claim: The estimator extends to several p-norm/discrete-volume families, but it is not universally consistent for correlated combinatorial data.
key_findings.evidence: Supplemental derivations give dimension-continuous volume expressions and error formulas. Spin-system tests in dimensions three and four are underestimated and fail the theoretical-versus-empirical CDF check, demonstrating that local Poisson/independence assumptions can be diagnosed rather than silently trusted.

key_findings.claim: A 16S metagenomic sequence example gives an effective local dimension around two, but the biological interpretation is exploratory.
key_findings.evidence: Applying I3D to a mutation/edit-like discrete metric yields a low estimate compatible across selected radii. The paper notes that genomic samples are not uniformly distributed lattice points, so the result describes local data geometry rather than a literal number of evolutionary variables.

method.core_idea: Replace infinitesimal continuous-volume scaling with a likelihood built from exact finite shell counts for the chosen discrete metric.
method.mechanism: For every point, the algorithm counts neighbors inside two radii, plugs an analytically continued discrete ball-volume ratio into a conditional binomial/Poisson likelihood, maximizes over dimension, and pools local contributions. Goodness-of-fit plots compare empirical and predicted count-ratio distributions to flag violations.
assumptions: Sampling density is approximately constant within the selected local neighborhood.
The metric's ball volume is known or accurately approximated as a smooth function of dimension.
Neighborhood counts behave approximately as independent Poisson samples after conditioning.
A single effective dimension is meaningful over the pooled data and radius window.

techniques.role: Represents staircase neighborhood growth without a zero-distance limit.
Infers dimension from inner versus outer shell occupancy.
Allows maximum-likelihood optimization over noninteger effective dimension.
Detects datasets and radii where the discrete Poisson model is inconsistent.

evaluations.setting: Uniform samples on two- and six-dimensional square lattices with periodic boundaries.
evaluations.metric: Bias and variability of estimated intrinsic dimension versus radius.
evaluations.result: I3D is closest to ground truth at small discrete radii and remains stable over a wider usable range than the compared continuous/fractal estimators.
evaluations.baseline: Continuous intrinsic-dimension, box-counting, and fractal-dimension estimators.

evaluations.setting: Discrete spin configurations and supplemental metric families.
evaluations.metric: Dimension error and empirical-versus-model CDF agreement.
evaluations.result: Some controlled metric families fit, but three- and four-dimensional spin systems are underestimated and fail validation, exposing correlated-neighborhood failure.
evaluations.baseline: Known ambient/intrinsic dimensions and the fitted I3D model.

evaluations.setting: 16S metagenomic sequences under a discrete mutation-distance construction.
evaluations.metric: Effective dimension stability across local radii and mappings.
evaluations.result: Estimates cluster near two for the chosen setup and vary only modestly under reported mapping/radius changes.
evaluations.baseline: Alternative radius choices and continuous estimators.

limitations: The correct ball-volume law must be available for the specific discrete metric.
Local constant density and count independence can fail badly in correlated structured data.
Radius selection is a bias-variance/model-validity tradeoff and is not fully automatic.
The genomics result is one exploratory dataset and does not establish a mechanistic biological dimension.
Pooling one dimension can hide heterogeneous or multifractal regions.
failure_modes: Ties and shell correlations can invalidate the Poisson/binomial likelihood.
Boundary effects distort ball volume when the data do not use periodic or sufficiently interior neighborhoods.
Metric mismatch can make the nominal discrete ball unrelated to semantic variation.
A validation plot may pass over one radius interval while dimension changes across scales.
reusable_insights: Intrinsic-dimension estimators should model the exact metric-volume law rather than assume Euclidean infinitesimals.
Publish a goodness-of-fit diagnostic with every dimension estimate.
Radius should be reported as a scale-dependent profile, not hidden after choosing one favorable value.
open_questions: Can discrete ball volumes be learned with uncertainty for edit, graph, or program metrics lacking closed forms?
How can correlated neighborhood counts be modeled without losing computational simplicity?
Can local heterogeneous I3D estimates reveal biologically meaningful submanifolds rather than one global number?

competitive_landscape.title: Estimating the intrinsic dimension of datasets by a minimal neighborhood information
competitive_landscape.relationship: Introduces TwoNN, a minimal nearest-neighbor ratio estimator for continuous manifold data.
competitive_landscape.difference: TwoNN assumes continuous distance ratios; I3D is designed for tied/staircase distances and replaces ratios with finite discrete shell counts.

competitive_landscape.title: The geometry of hidden representations of large transformer models
competitive_landscape.relationship: Uses continuous TwoNN estimates to diagnose representation manifolds across transformer layers.
competitive_landscape.difference: It is an application to Euclidean activations; the discrete-metric paper develops a new estimator for combinatorial distance spaces and explicitly validates its count model.

competitive_landscape.title: Learning to Compress: Local Rank and Information Compression in Deep Neural Networks
competitive_landscape.relationship: Provides a local-rank alternative for quantifying effective representation dimension and compression.
competitive_landscape.difference: Local rank works through continuous representation spectra; I3D targets datasets where only a discrete metric and shell occupancy are meaningful.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: I3D is an intrinsic-dimension estimator specifically derived for discrete metrics and finite shell-volume scaling.
novelty_assessment.evidence: Likelihood derivation, exact/continued volume laws, synthetic comparisons, explicit model checks, and a genomic case distinguish it from continuous nearest-neighbor methods.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The metric-aware likelihood and falsifiable fit diagnostic are strong contributions; applicability is bounded by available volume models and local count independence.
